transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi. Um… I’m here because my eating has gotten kind of out of hand, I guess. Especially at night. Like after everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have a little bit of leftovers, and then suddenly I’ve eaten… way more than that. Half a tray of catered pasta from work, dessert left over from a client dinner, whatever snacks are in the pantry.

It’s embarrassing to say out loud. I work in marketing, so there are always client dinners and catered things around, and honestly sometimes I’m thinking more about what’s coming home in the takeout containers than the meeting itself, which sounds awful. But yeah… it’s usually in one sitting, and then I’m sitting there wondering how it even happened.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

I… don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I feel awful afterward and I’ll make all these big promises to myself, like “tomorrow I’ll be normal,” and then I get caught up thinking about work clothes fitting tighter or how I have this presentation coming up and—sorry, I’m getting off track.

I haven’t really… I don’t think I do those things in some organized way. I mostly just feel guilty and try to move on, I guess.
During these episodes when you eat a lot, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah… yes, that’s probably the part that scares me the most. Once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night with my husband, it’s like the decision-making part of me just goes offline.

I’ll literally be thinking, “Patricia, stop, this is enough,” and my hand is still reaching for more. And then I’ll start telling myself, “Well, you already messed it up, so just finish it,” which is—sorry, that sounds ridiculous when I say it. But in the moment it doesn’t feel like I’m choosing normally.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like affecting your work, relationships, or how you feel about yourself?

Yeah… it does. I mean, I’m still functioning at work, mostly. I still show up, I still get the decks done and answer emails and do the meetings. People probably wouldn’t know.

But the mornings after it happens, I feel just… heavy, drained, ashamed. Like I’m dragging myself through the day. And then I start canceling things I normally like—yoga, or time I’d set aside to draw or do something creative—because I don’t want to be seen, or I don’t want to have to explain why I’m so off.

And then of course canceling makes me feel worse, because those are the things that usually help me feel like myself. So yes, it’s affecting me, even if I’m still technically keeping everything together.
Do these episodes of eating a lot happen in specific, distinct times — like within a couple of hours or less — or does it feel more like you're just eating heavily throughout the whole evening?

It’s more like a distinct time, I think. Like… it’s not that I’m grazing all night from dinner onward, exactly.

A lot of times it’s after everyone goes to bed, and I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers. And then suddenly it’s not just leftovers — it’s, you know, half a tray of catered pasta from work, and maybe the dessert I brought home from a client dinner, and then I’m opening the pantry for whatever snacks are there.

And it feels like one sitting. I mean, I’m not timing it with a stopwatch, but it’s definitely this contained episode, not just normal eating spread out over the whole evening.
